from collections import Counter
# Record demo grids, compactly recreated from received examples for validation.
d1=[[8,0,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,8,0,8] for _ in range(27)]
for r in [1,9,17,25]:
    color=3 if r in [1,9] else 2
    d1[r]=[0]*18; d1[r][1]=d1[r][16]=color
# reset other rows properly: background 8, vertical rails 0
for r in range(27):
    if r not in [1,9,17,25]:
        d1[r]=[8]*18; d1[r][1]=d1[r][16]=0

d2=[[6 if c%4!=3 else 4 for c in range(25)] for r in range(24)]
# vertical separators at c=3,7,11,15,19,23 colored 4
for r in range(24):
    for c in [3,7,11,15,19,23]: d2[r][c]=4
# horizontal separators at r=2,7,12,17,22 colored 4
for r in [2,7,12,17,22]:
    for c in range(25): d2[r][c]=4
# intersections marker lattice from demo
lat=[[2,2,2,4,4,4],[2,2,2,7,7,4],[0,0,7,7,7,4],[0,0,7,7,0,0],[4,4,4,4,0,0]]
for i,r in enumerate([2,7,12,17,22]):
    for j,c in enumerate([3,7,11,15,19,23]): d2[r][c]=lat[i][j]

def transform(grid):
    h,w=len(grid),len(grid[0])
    bg=Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    rows=[r for r,row in enumerate(grid) if sum(v!=bg for v in row)>w/2]
    cols=[c for c in range(w) if sum(grid[r][c]!=bg for r in range(h))>h/2]
    # most frequent non-background value along selected separator lines, excluding crossings
    sepvals=[]
    for r in rows:
        sepvals.extend(grid[r][c] for c in range(w) if c not in cols and grid[r][c]!=bg)
    for c in cols:
        sepvals.extend(grid[r][c] for r in range(h) if r not in rows and grid[r][c]!=bg)
    sep=Counter(sepvals).most_common(1)[0][0]
    out=[]
    for i in range(len(rows)-1):
        outrow=[]
        for j in range(len(cols)-1):
            corners=[grid[r][c] for r in [rows[i],rows[i+1]] for c in [cols[j],cols[j+1]]]
            vals=set(x for x in corners if x!=sep)
            outrow.append(next(iter(vals)) if len(vals)==1 else bg)
        out.append(outrow)
    return out
print('d1',transform(d1))
print('d2',transform(d2))

source='''from collections import Counter

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # The most common color fills the rectangular cells between separator lines.
    background = Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    # Separator rows and columns are the long, mostly non-background lines.
    sep_rows = [r for r, row in enumerate(grid)
                if sum(v != background for v in row) > w / 2]
    sep_cols = [c for c in range(w)
                if sum(grid[r][c] != background for r in range(h)) > h / 2]
    # Find the ordinary separator color away from intersections.
    line_colors = []
    for r in sep_rows:
        line_colors.extend(grid[r][c] for c in range(w)
                           if c not in sep_cols and grid[r][c] != background)
    for c in sep_cols:
        line_colors.extend(grid[r][c] for r in range(h)
                           if r not in sep_rows and grid[r][c] != background)
    separator = Counter(line_colors).most_common(1)[0][0]

    # A cell is colored only when its four corner markers all agree;
    # otherwise it keeps the interior background color.
    output = []
    for i in range(len(sep_rows) - 1):
        row = []
        for j in range(len(sep_cols) - 1):
            corners = [grid[sep_rows[i]][sep_cols[j]],
                       grid[sep_rows[i]][sep_cols[j + 1]],
                       grid[sep_rows[i + 1]][sep_cols[j]],
                       grid[sep_rows[i + 1]][sep_cols[j + 1]]]
            if corners[0] != separator and len(set(corners)) == 1:
                row.append(corners[0])
            else:
                row.append(background)
        output.append(row)
    return output
'''
p.write_text(source)
print('saved',p)
